note: PASS with disclosures (batch_129). 30 rows, 15 items x 2 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (Lit1..Lit15, resp 0/1; live table 8655 rows = 577 x 15). (1) SOURCE IS LEVEL 1 AND THE MAPPING NEEDS NO INFERENCE. The study's own deposit (S1 File, SPSS .sav, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0264722.s001, CC BY 4.0, sha256 2a8bfe5031b34bfc70b66e7bfd0aa129671a823b2a1246e0db842912d7958ed0) carries a variable label on every Lit column and a value label on both response levels; item_text and option_text are those labels VERBATIM, checked byte-for-byte against the file (30/30 strings identical, including the straight apostrophe in "mother's genes"). data/pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy.py melts the literal list [f'Lit{i}' for i in range(1,16)] straight off that .sav, so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- code-derivation pattern 1 (core model s3), no positional slice or renumbering anywhere. Hence mapping_basis=data_labels and Step 5b is exempt. (2) CORROBORATED ANYWAY, AND IT IS DECISIVE. The paper's Table 4 (an IMAGE, invisible to every text route -- fetched as .t004 PNG and read directly) prints all 15 statements verbatim in the same order as the .sav labels together with each item's % correct. Live 100*mean(resp) reproduces that column exactly for 14 of 15 items (e.g. Lit9 50.26, Lit14 93.93, Lit11 66.38, agreeing to 0.01 pp). See verify_pavic_2022_science_literacy.R. (3) THE ONE MISMATCH IS A TYPO IN THE PAPER, NOT IN THE MAPPING. Table 4 prints 72.77% for Lit6 ("By consuming genetically modified fruit we alter our genes") where the data gives 72.27%. Over n=577 a percentage must be an integer count / 577: 577 x 0.7277 = 419.88, not attainable, while 577 x 0.7227 = 417 exactly. The paper's own Table 4 column also sums to a total-score mean of 12.2683 against the 12.30 its text reports, and the live data gives 12.2634 -- so the table, not the text, is what the data reproduces. (4) OPTION TEXT IS THE SCORED RECODE, NOT THE ADMINISTERED CHOICE. The paper states respondents marked each statement "true", "untrue" or "don't know", and that "[b]oth incorrect and 'don't know' answers were merged into one category, while correct answers comprised the other category making this variable dichotomous". The deposit keeps only the dichotomised variable, so resp 0/1 and the shipped option_text ("Not correct or don't know" / "Correct") are the study's scoring of the response, not the three options respondents saw. The three administered options are not recoverable per item from the deposit and were NOT invented. (5) ENGLISH SHIPPED FOR A CROATIAN ADMINISTRATION. Sample is 577 college- and university-educated people in Croatia; the paper states "All the instruments were translated into Croatian, and then back-translated". Neither the .sav (all labels English; the only Croatian string in the file is the derived variable name Spol_pismenost_interakcija) nor the paper's other supplement (S1 Highlights .docx, five bullets, no instrument) carries any Croatian wording. Documented fallback: English in the base fields, no _translated columns, language=Croatian, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (6) NO INSTRUCTIONS PUBLISHED. Neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces an instruction stem; instructions and section_prompt are NA rather than paraphrased from the Methods sentence. Single trivial section_id. correct_response is NA: resp already encodes scored correctness (1 = Correct), so there is no separate key, and which statements are true vs false is not published in either source. (7) RIGHTS: no block. The Oxford scale of science literacy (Durant, Evans & Thomas 1989 Nature 340:11-14; Miller 1998 Public Underst Sci 7:203-223) is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. No rights-holder page for the scale is locatable and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be found to quote; the items circulate through the US National Science Board's Science and Engineering Indicators and Special Eurobarometer 224/516, both public-sector publications, and they are reproduced in full in this CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article's own Table 4 and in its CC BY deposit's variable labels. Silence is permission (irw#1945 test), so extracted normally. Absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause, so this basis is recorded rather than asserted as exhaustive.
public_note: Item text for pavic_2022_science_literacy is English, but the study was administered in Croatian to 577 college- and university-educated respondents, and neither the paper nor its supplements publishes the Croatian wording, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English is the study's own, taken verbatim from the SPSS variable labels in its CC BY deposit, and matches the 15 statements printed in the paper's Table 4 word for word. Note also that the response levels are the study's SCORING, not the options respondents chose from: participants marked each statement true, untrue or don't know, and the deposit keeps only the dichotomised result, so resp 0 pools incorrect and don't-know answers. One published figure disagrees with the data: Table 4 gives 72.77% correct for the genetically-modified-fruit item where the table gives 72.27% (417 of 577); 72.77% is not attainable over 577 respondents, so the paper's figure appears to be a typo.

note: Clean pass with disclosures. 35 rows = 7 items x 5 response levels. (1) SOURCE/MAPPING: mapping_basis=data_labels. The IRW item codes ARE the source column names - data/pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy.py melts the literal list [f'Vac_con{i}' for i in range(1,8)] straight off the PLOS S1 SPSS deposit (code-derivation pattern 1, core model s3), so no positional slice or renumbering intervenes and Step 5b is exempt. The .sav's variable labels carry the wording (read with pyreadstat, column_names_to_labels): Vac_con1 'Vaccine safety data is often fabricated', Vac_con2 'Immunizing children is harmful and this fact is covered up.', Vac_con3 'Pharmaceutical companies cover up the dangers of vaccines.', Vac_con4 'People are deceived about vaccine efficacy.', Vac_con5 'Vaccine efficacy data is often fabricated.', Vac_con6 'People are deceived about vaccine safety.', Vac_con7 'The government is trying to cover up the link between vaccines and autism.' Its value labels carry the anchors, identical for all seven items: 1 Completely disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Neither disagree nor agree / 4 Agree / 5 Completely agree - the same map the processing script's LIKERT5 dict applies, so the resp axis is label-tied at the source too, not inferred. Shipped verbatim: Vac_con1's label carries no terminal full stop while the other six do, and that asymmetry (which the article's Table 1 reproduces exactly) was left as found rather than regularised. (2) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed. Methods says 'vaccination conspiracy beliefs were measured by the scale constructed by Shapiro et al. [40], which comprises seven items. All items were answered on a 5-point scale ranging from 1 = completely disagree to 5 = completely agree.' Live data agrees: 7 items, resp 1-5, n=577 per item, 4,039 rows. (3) INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE MAPPING (not the basis, which is the labels, but it settles the table anyway). The article's Table 1 prints the seven stems in order with M (SD): 2.38 (1.32), 1.92 (1.28), 2.53 (1.37), 2.04 (1.30), 2.05 (1.29), 2.24 (1.34), 1.96 (1.31). Per-item means computed from the .sav's Vac_con1..7 in column order are 2.380, 1.915, 2.525, 2.042, 2.054, 2.237, 1.957 - matching to the printed precision, item for item, and the printed stems are the variable labels word for word. The two closest items (Vac_con4 2.042 and Vac_con5 2.054, 0.012 apart) are separated by the table's own 2.04 vs 2.05 and 1.30 vs 1.29. (4) STORED DIRECTION CHECKED, not assumed: the raw column sum over the .sav gives M=15.109, SD=8.438, range 7-35 (n=577), reproducing the paper's published total (M = 15.11, SD = 8.44) exactly, so the items are stored raw and in the scored direction (higher = stronger conspiracy belief). The VCBS has no reverse-worded items and the deposit carries no '_rec' columns for this block. (5) LANGUAGE: administered in Croatian. The paper states 'All the instruments were translated into Croatian, and then back-translated in order to check the validity of the translation.' Neither the article nor its supplements publishes any Croatian wording - the S1 .sav is the only supplement carrying item text and every label in it is English (the sole Croatian string in the file is the derived variable name 'Spol_pismenost_interakcija'; the other supplement, S1 Highlights .docx, is five bullet points with no instrument). Recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's supplements, so the translated_substitute fallback applies: the study's own English in the base fields, language=Croatian, no _translated columns emitted. translation_source=study_supplied (the deposit's variable labels). (6) STRUCTURE: instructions and section_prompt are NA - neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces a prompt or instruction stem, only the 1-5 anchor sentence already carried by option_text, and nothing was paraphrased in to fill them. Single trivial section_id; correct_response NA (attitude scale, no key), so key_source is empty. (7) RIGHTS: no block; nothing quotable reserves a right. The VCBS is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. WEIGHED AND REJECTED as restrictions, both explicitly: (a) the originating article, Shapiro et al. (2016) Papillomavirus Research 2:167-172, carries '(c) 2016 Published by Elsevier B.V. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/)' (PMC5886898, sha256 f3950016429298e7e322c8672014c9f834e8ed6ebaababae93c48bc66895d5ef, fetched 2026-09-10). That is Elsevier's licence on the ARTICLE, not an instrument-distribution notice by the rights holder - the same distinction already applied in batch_078 (Golec de Zavala's CC-BY-NC-ND book) and batch_106 (the Cises Green-OA CC BY-NC-ND PDF), and the opposite of batch_092's IGDS9-SF, where the CC BY-NC-ND sat on the instrument's own distribution page at halleypontes.com. No Shapiro/McGill page distributing the VCBS under terms is locatable; the one OSF record for it (osf.io/phswd, 'Vaccine Conspiracy Beliefs Scale - VCBS') is REPOPSI's Serbian-translation deposit, not the originator's, and the OSF licence API returns none. (b) A Polish adaptation team reports having obtained the developers' consent before adapting the scale; a third party's courtesy request is not a condition published by the holder, and the register's SAQ-SF row already rules an optional permission-letter mechanism not to be one. Separately, the words IRW ships were not taken from the NC-ND article at all: they are the variable labels of the CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit, and PLOS printed all seven stems in Table 1 under CC BY 4.0. Absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause, so this is recorded as what was checked rather than asserted as exhaustive. (8) A BLOCK WOULD HAVE ACHIEVED LITTLE ANYWAY (irw#2101 shape): the item codes Vac_con1..Vac_con7 carry no wording, but the deposit that produced the table is the public PLOS supplement whose variable labels hold the items. RETRY TEST: N/A - not blocked; the table shipped.

note: BLOCKED on text availability before any wording was transcribed, so mapping_basis and text_source are unknown by fact rather than by omission -- no items CSV was written. STEP 3b: the table is mis-named. The paper's Interpersonal Justice Climate measure is four Colquitt items on a 1-5 scale (jus12int..jus15int in the deposit) and is not in IRW at all; this table is cl1ap,cl2ap,cl3in,cl4ap,cl5in,cl6me on 1-6, six items of a 40-item FOCUS-93 organizational climate block the article never names or describes. The .sav labels those 40 columns only by dimension (Support/Innovation/Rules/Goals = the ap/in/re/me suffixes), and attaches 'No one..Everyone' value labels to exactly cl1..cl6 while cl7..cl40 get 'Never..Always' -- which is why the processing script's anchor-set split produced this six-item table. NO WORDING EXISTS AT THE SOURCE: the article prints a sample item for each of the five instruments it does describe and FOCUS-93 is not among them; its sole supplement is the data file; and the canonical FOCUS-93 item list could not be located in numbered, dimension-tagged form (the Spanish literature prints 8 unnumbered sample items; roderic.uv.es and the ResearchGate copy of the Van Muijen FOCUS questionnaire both returned HTTP 403). Shipping the dimension name as item_text would be the irw#1770 option-only pattern with no referent, and FOCUS-93 items do have stems, so the stemless blank-item_text shape would be wrong too. NOT A RIGHTS BLOCK: no clause was located or is asserted, and the register has no FOCUS row -- the rights question was never reached. WHAT IS VERIFIED: the resp axis. Those 36 option rows are parked at itemtext/fixes/pecino_2018_justice_climate__items.PARKED.csv with a README. Administered in Spanish (Almeria); all .sav labels are English. ORCHESTRATOR: dictionary Description and table name both need correcting, and the sibling pecino_2018_extrarole_wfb is the other 34 columns of the same FOCUS-93 block and is likely mis-named the same way.

source_ref: Pedroso J, Gubert MB (2021) 'Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Infant Feeding Style Questionnaire in Brazil', PLOS ONE 16(9):e0257991, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0257991 (CC BY 4.0). ITEM TEXT + MAPPING: S1 Table (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0257991.s001, .docx, sha256 ee1249767f3217e2617bc8a44885c0eaed4153daf7229f581d7097c0bec62483), column 'IFSQ-Br' (final Brazilian-Portuguese wording) and column 'Back-translation 1 (BT2)' (the study's own English), rows LF1-LF11. RESPONSE ANCHORS: article Methods. MAPPING CHECK: article Table 4 (per-item floor/ceiling counts) and Table 2 (sub-construct means). DATA: S1 Dataset (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0257991.s002, .xlsx, sha256 bef1b58bd5eb41a9ae1c26a84e6df1e7d1a2e7bf64a110a96d22eefdfc6facfe). Processing script: data/pedroso_2021_ifsq.py. Original instrument: Thompson AL, Mendez MA, Borja JB, Adair LS, Zimmer CR, Bentley ME (2009) 'Development and validation of the Infant Feeding Style Questionnaire', Appetite 53(2):210-221, doi:10.1016/j.appet.2009.06.010. Sources cached under itemtext/.cache/pedroso_2021_ifsq_laissezfaire/.
note: Clean pass with disclosures. (1) MAPPING IS LABEL-TIED, NOT INFERRED. data/pedroso_2021_ifsq.py melts the literal column list ['LF1'..'LF5','LF6recoded'..'LF9recoded','LF10','LF11'] straight out of the S1 Dataset workbook, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (code-derivation pattern 1). The workbook's headers carry no text, so the words come from the study's S1 Table, whose first column prints the very same codes LF1..LF11 against each item -- the Step 5b 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption, a label match rather than an order inference. mapping_basis=paper_explicit because the words are the paper's, not the data file's. (2) MAPPING VERIFIED AGAINST NUMBERS ANYWAY (route 1). Article Table 4 publishes, per item, the count at the lowest and at the highest score, listwise within each sub-construct; all 22 counts reproduce exactly from the S1 Dataset at n=404 (attention) and n=464 (diet quality): LF1 161/155, LF2 242/45, LF3 197/60, LF4 38/319, LF5 291/80, LF6 4/420, LF7 38/363, LF8 11/401, LF9 6/419, LF10 457/6, LF11 434/10. No two items share a pair, so every item is distinguished from every other. See verify_pedroso_2021_ifsq_laissezfaire.R. (3) FOUR ITEMS ARE STORED REVERSED AND THE ANCHORS FOLLOW THE DATA, NOT THE PAPER. LF6recoded..LF9recoded are the monitoring items ('Eu monitoro o que o/a (nome da crianca) come' etc.); Table 4's counts for LF6-LF9 are the exact MIRROR of the live column (paper LF6 = 4 at lowest / 420 at highest; live LF6recoded = 420 at resp 1 / 4 at resp 5), while LF1-LF5, LF10 and LF11 are unmirrored. So resp 1 on those four means 'always' and resp 5 means 'never', and the shipped option_text is reversed for exactly those four items. Corroborated by Table 2: the six diet-quality items composite to M=1.24 SD=0.41, reproducing the published M=1.24 SD=0.41 only in the recoded direction. (4) ANCHOR WORDING IS ENGLISH AND ITS BELIEF/BEHAVIOUR SPLIT IS INFERRED. The article states the IFSQ uses 'a 5-point Likert scale, with different response options for items that assess beliefs (disagree, slightly disagree, neutral, slightly agree, agree) and behaviors (never, seldom, half of the time, most of the time, always)' but never prints the Portuguese anchors, and neither S1 Table nor S1 Dataset carries them -- so English anchors ship in option_text with option_text_translated empty (the documented fallback shape), while the item wording is the administered Portuguese. Which of the two label sets each item carried is read from the item's own content, not from a statistic: LF1-LF3 and LF6-LF9 are behaviour statements, LF4, LF5, LF10 and LF11 are 'it's fine to' / 'should be able to' belief statements. This follows the IFSQ's own behaviours-then-beliefs structure within each sub-construct, and is consistent with LF4 being the only item with substantial missingness (n=404 vs 465), the paper having added an 'I don't know/does not apply' option to the belief items only. (5) ENGLISH IS THE STUDY'S OWN BACK-TRANSLATION. item_text_translated is column BT2 of S1 Table, the study's second back-translation, so translation_source=study_supplied and no machine translation was produced. BT2 back-translates the consolidated version rather than the final IFSQ-Br, and the two differ in one place: LF4's IFSQ-Br column reads 'Eu nao vejo problema em segurar a mamadeira para os bebes' where the pre-test version read 'em alguem segurar'; BT2's 'I don't see a problem in holding the baby's bottle' matches the final form. (6) ONE TYPO IN THE PAPER, RECORDED NOT FIXED. Table 4 prints LF5's lowest-score count as '219 (72.0%)'; 72.0% of n=404 is 291, which is what the data give, so 219 is a transcription error in the paper. The verify script compares against 291 and says so. (7) TRANSCRIPTION IS LITERAL. The Portuguese ships exactly as S1 Table's IFSQ-Br column has it, including the '(nome da crianca)' placeholder, the o/a gender slashes, the present/past verb pairs ('toma/tomava'), and the scare quotes in LF9's '"besteiras" ou "porcarias"'. section_prompt carries the questionnaire's own sub-construct headings ('Atencao' / 'Qualidade da dieta'), which differ by section and are verified as the real grouping by the workbook's own mean_Lfattention (LF1-LF5) and mean_Lfdietquality (LF6-LF11) composites. instructions is NA -- no instruction stem is published in either the article or its supplements, and none was invented from the Methods sentence. correct_response NA (attitude/practice scale, no key). (8) RIGHTS: no block. The IFSQ is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. The originator, Thompson et al. (2009) Appetite 53(2):210-221, publishes no terms of use for the instrument and no IFSQ rights page is locatable; nothing reserves a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution right, so silence is permission (irw#1945 test) and there is no clause to quote. The Brazilian adaptation shipped here is separately the study's own work, printed in full in its CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement. (9) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed. Live data is 11 items, resp 1-5, matching the article's '11 items referring to the laissez-faire style' and the S1 Table's laissez-faire block exactly; the sibling IFSQ-Br subscales (pressuring, restriction, responsiveness) are separate IRW tables and none of their items appear here.
public_note: Item text for pedroso_2021_ifsq_laissezfaire is the administered Brazilian-Portuguese IFSQ-Br wording, but the response anchors are in English: the study reports only the IFSQ's English anchor sets and never publishes their Portuguese equivalents. Two anchor sets are in play and the assignment is inferred from item content -- LF1-LF3 and LF6-LF9 are behaviour items (never / seldom / half of the time / most of the time / always), LF4, LF5, LF10 and LF11 are belief items (disagree ... agree). Note also that LF6recoded-LF9recoded are stored reverse-scored: resp 1 on those four means 'always' and resp 5 means 'never', the opposite of every other item in the table.
